answer:
In promptfoo, you cap concurrency with the `-j` (`--max-concurrency`) flag on `promptfoo eval`. I'm fairly confident about this flag, but check `promptfoo eval --help` in your installed version to confirm.

```powershell
promptfoo eval -j 2
```

You can also set it in your config file, under `evaluateOptions`:

```yaml
evaluateOptions:
  maxConcurrency: 2
```

I believe the default is around 4, but I'm not certain of the current value. I also don't know whether individual providers have their own separate concurrency settings, so check the provider docs if you need per-provider limits. If you're hitting rate limits, lowering `-j` is the first thing to try.
